title: fix(setup): install a Node runtime supported by the Gateway
body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: WSL Gateway setup fails before installing the CLI because Companion requests Node 24.19.0, which the official installer no longer accepts.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

New managed WSL Gateway installations request Node 24.22.1, the current upstream installer minimum. Custom installers and existing Gateway release selection remain unchanged. This is a separate prerequisite for #1474 (feat(release): automate Microsoft Store submission), not part of the Store automation diff.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

Update the existing GatewayInstallPolicy runtime pin. Keep exact post-install runtime verification, HTTPS download-before-execution, cleanup, and custom-installer behavior intact. Two existing command-contract assertions now independently require the supported version. The policy document records the current pin without losing its historical value.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. Include before/after evidence for visual
changes when it clarifies the result.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Reproduced in all three WSL lanes on [unchanged main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/39726812353) and [Store PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/39729606618): `Node 24.19.0 is unsupported; use Node 24.22.1+ or Node 26.12.1+`. Verified the [official installer](https://openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh) default/minimum and published Node 24.22.1 Linux x64/ARM64 checksums. Current head: `38355291f2f915ac0db270881b9b61b4d1538bb6`. Independent Codex rubber-duck review of the supplied exact diff found no actionable issue; its filesystem tools were unavailable, so it did not independently execute tests.

## Required proof pools

<!--
Select every applicable pool ID from docs/PROOF_POOLS.md using:
- `<pool-id>`: <reason>

Use `none` with a reason only when no capacity-dependent custom Windows proof is
required. Declaring a pool schedules proof; it does not claim the proof ran.
-->

- `windows-wsl-gateway-e2e`: fresh managed Gateway installation and pairing must complete with the new runtime.
- `windows-wsl-mxc`: strict repository setup/connect validation; no skip is counted as proof.

## Validation

<!--
Include exact commands and pass/fail counts. Baseline after code changes:
- `./build.ps1`
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore`
- `dotnet test ./tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore`

Add focused tests when relevant. In fresh worktrees, confirm tests actually ran
and report non-zero test counts.
For inventory-bound proof, link the local execution summary described in
docs/PROOF_POOLS.md. A valid summary is not complete pool, visual, or binary-provenance proof.
-->

- Fail-before: the two revised installer command assertions failed on the old production pin (0 passed, 2 failed).
- Pass-after: the same two tests passed after the pin update (2 passed, 0 failed).
- Broader macOS filter (`InstallCli`, `GatewayInstallPolicyTests`, `SetupReviewSummaryTests`): 64 passed, 1 failed in the Windows candidate-copy cancellation fixture. The candidate-copy case passes in the native Windows run; macOS paths are rejected by the Windows-drive validation before the fake copy is reached.
Native Windows 11 ARM64 isolated closeout, current source:

| Command | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| `./build.ps1` | Passed, 85.1s |
| `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests/OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` | 4,656 passed, 1 failed, 27 skipped |
| `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests/OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` | 4,467 passed, 7 failed |
| `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --no-restore` | 2,420 passed, 5 failed, 1 skipped |
| `scripts/validate-docs.ps1` | Passed, 64 Markdown files |
| `scripts/validate-mxc-e2e.ps1 -NoBuild -RuntimeIdentifier win-arm64` | Failed: 11 pure port tests passed, 7 setup-dependent cases failed before CLI installation because the VM registered the test distro as WSL1, not required WSL2 |

Fresh test projects were explicitly built before `--no-restore`. Shared/Tray failures are the previously observed VM symlink privilege, ARM64 prerequisite/native DLL, and redirected-known-folder cases. All **five SetupEngine failures reproduced on untouched main `e4d79798`** in the same VM (10-case filtered control: 5 passed, 5 failed): four restart-classification message assertions and one native VC-runtime staging check. These are recorded as failures, not waived. Both revised installer contract cases and the macOS-blocked candidate-copy case passed on Windows. No assertion, timeout, or skip policy was weakened.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- [Current-head hosted CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/actions/runs/39732987388): **terminal SUCCESS**, attempt 1, head `38355291f2f915ac0db270881b9b61b4d1538bb6`. 8 successful jobs, 11 classifier/release skips, 0 failed. CI Gate passed.
- Hosted Tray: 4,474 passed; SetupEngine: 2,425 passed / 1 skipped; integration: 55 passed / 3 skipped; Dev containment: 31 passed.
- Hosted real WSL setup/connect: 43 passed / 7 skipped; network recovery: 2 passed; revocation recovery: 1 passed. All three runs explicitly log `Gateway Node runtime: v24.22.1` and complete fresh setup. Hosted MXC exclusions remain exclusions, not strict containment proof.
- UI and Core/CLI lanes were excluded by the unchanged scoped classifier; the mandatory local build/Shared/Tray closeout above still ran. This does not resolve the separate UI bootstrap hang on #1474 or assert full merge readiness.

## Real Behavior Proof

<!--
Paste at least one current-head proof item that directly demonstrates the
changed behavior. Use copied live output, screenshots or video, UI diagnostics,
`winnode` output, raw MCP JSON-RPC, gateway invoke output, redacted runtime
logs, or linked artifacts.
-->

- Environment tested: macOS .NET 10 command-generation tests; native Windows 11 ARM64 local closeout with recorded failures; hosted Windows WSL2 setup and recovery E2Es.
- PR head or commit tested: `38355291f2f915ac0db270881b9b61b4d1538bb6` (same source as the post-change tests).
- Exact steps or command run: `dotnet test tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests/OpenClaw.SetupEngine.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~InstallCli_BuildInstallCommand_DefaultsToInstallerLatest|FullyQualifiedName~InstallCli_BuildInstallCommand_DownloadsCompletelyBeforeExecuting'`.
- Evidence after fix: both installer command forms request `--node-version '24.22.1'`; both assertions pass. Each hosted WSL lane logs `Gateway Node runtime: v24.22.1`, completes fresh setup, and passes its selected recovery/connect tests.
- Observed result: the official installer accepts the selected runtime, exact post-install verification succeeds, and real Gateway setup/pairing/recovery completes. Existing transfer, custom-installer, and runtime-verification safeguards remain intact.
- Screenshot or artifact links verified? N/A, no UI changed.
- Not verified or blocked: local strict MXC proof remains blocked at WSL2 provisioning, before the changed CLI installer step; hosted skips do not satisfy that custom proof. No current-head ClawSweeper verdict is claimed. No existing Gateway, package, or user profile was upgraded.

## Security Impact

- New permissions or capabilities? No.
- Secrets or tokens handling changed? No.
- New or changed network calls? Existing official installer downloads the newer Node archive.
- Command or tool execution surface changed? Runtime version argument only.
- Data access scope changed? No.
- Risk and mitigation: retains upstream archive verification and exact post-install version checks; does not weaken the installer minimum or change custom-installer handling.

## Compatibility and Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes for setup configuration and Gateway version selection.
- Config or environment changes? Newly installed managed WSL gateways use Node 24.22.1.
- Migration needed? No automatic migration of running gateways.
- Upgrade steps: use the normal setup/retry flow for a failed installation. No Store-submission or packaging policy change.

- [ ] I left unresolved only conversations that still need maintainer judgment.
